# package eds

```go
import "github.com/otfabric/go-ethernetip/eds"
```

Package eds reads, validates, writes and generates Electronic Data Sheets: the text files (.eds) in which a device vendor describes an EtherNet/IP device's identity, parameters, assemblies and I/O connections.

[Parse](#func-parse) reads a file into its sections and entries without interpreting them, so that vendor-specific sections survive a round trip through [File.Format](#func-file-format). The typed views ([File.Device](#func-file-device), [File.Params](#func-file-params), [File.Assemblies](#func-file-assemblies), [File.Connections](#func-file-connections)) interpret the public sections; [Validate](#func-validate) checks a file against the rules of the format; [GenerateGo](#func-generatego) turns a file into Go constants, types and scanner configurations.

The grammar follows the publicly documented EDS format as the eds\_pie project (MIT) and vendor EDS files use it; the ODVA specification of EDS (CIP Volume 1, chapter 7) is not available to this project.

## Constants

```go
const MaxAssemblySize = 0xFFFF
```

MaxAssemblySize is the largest assembly size, in octets, an EDS can declare: the size field is 16 bits. A member larger than that, in bits 8\*MaxAssemblySize, is rejected.

```go
const (
	MaxFileSize = 16 << 20 // octets
	// fields of one entry
	// entries of the file
)
```

Limits that bound what Parse accepts from an untrusted file.

## Functions

### func FormatEPATH

```go
func FormatEPATH(p cip.Path) (string, error)
```

FormatEPATH writes a path as an EDS EPATH.

### func GenerateGo

```go
func GenerateGo(f *File, opts GenerateOptions) ([]byte, error)
```

GenerateGo generates Go source for the device an EDS describes:

  - its identity as constants and its electronic key;
  - a constant and a descriptor per parameter, with a range check, and a type with named constants per enumerated parameter;
  - per assembly its instance and size and, when its members are whole octets of parameters with numeric types, a struct with Encode and Decode methods;
  - per I/O connection whose path names assembly points, a function that returns its scanner.IOConfig.

The output is gofmt-formatted and deterministic: the same file gives the same source. Validate the file first: GenerateGo fails on the errors that prevent generation and skips what it cannot express, saying so in a comment.

### func ParseEPATH

```go
func ParseEPATH(s string) (cip.Path, error)
```

ParseEPATH parses the EPATH of an EDS: hex octets separated by spaces, "20 04 24 64 2C 65". It is packed (no pad octets).

### type Connection

```go
type Connection struct {
	Number int
	// TriggerTransport and Params are the two bit-mask fields.
	TriggerTransport uint32
	Params           uint32
	// OTRPI and TORPI are the RPI fields: a number of microseconds, a
	// ParamN reference, or empty.
	OTRPI, TORPI string
	// OTSize, TOSize, OTFormat and TOFormat are the size and format
	// fields: numbers, ParamN or AssemN references, or empty.
	OTSize, OTFormat string
	TOSize, TOFormat string
	ConfigSize       string

	Name             string
	Help             string

	PathText string

```

#### func (Connection) Class

```go
func (c Connection) Class() int
```

Class returns the transport class of the trigger and transport mask: bits 0..15 flag classes 0 to 15 (CIP Volume 1, 7-3.6.13 as EDS files use it); the lowest flagged class is returned.

#### func (Field) String

```go
func (f Field) String() string
```

String returns the field as it is written in a file. A string is quoted with its quotes and backslashes escaped; an EDS string has no escape for a newline, so a string field must hold one line ([Build](#func-build) refuses control characters).

### type FieldKind

```go
type FieldKind uint8
```

FieldKind is how a field was written.

```go
const (
	// FieldEmpty is a field left empty between two commas.
	FieldEmpty FieldKind = iota
	// FieldString is a quoted string; adjacent strings are joined.
	FieldString
	// FieldToken is an unquoted token: a number, a keyword, a date, a
	// time, a reference such as Param3.
	FieldToken
	// FieldDataset is a braced list, written {a, b, c}.
	FieldDataset
)
```

Field kinds.

#### func Build

```go
func Build(s Spec) (*File, error)
```

Build returns an EDS file for a device: [File](#type-file), [Device](#type-device), \[Device Classification], \[Params] (the RPI parameter), [Assembly](#type-assembly) and \[Connection Manager]. The trigger and parameter masks of the connections are those of a Class 1 cyclic point-to-point connection with a fixed size, as common EDS files have them; review them against your device.

#### func Parse

```go
func Parse(r io.Reader) (*File, error)
```

Parse reads an EDS file. Comments ($ to the end of the line) are dropped. It reads at most MaxFileSize octets.

#### func (File) Format

```go
func (f *File) Format() string
```

Format writes the file in canonical form: sections in their order, entries with their fields, one field per line for long entries. Comments are not kept. Format(Parse(x)) is stable: formatting the result again changes nothing.

### type Issue


Issue is a finding of [Validate](#func-validate).

#### func Validate

```go
func Validate(f *File) []Issue
```

Validate checks a file and returns its issues, errors first. A file with no Error issue can be used by the typed views and the generator.

It checks: [File](#type-file) and [Device](#type-device) come first, with their required entries; dates, times and revisions are well formed; numbers are numbers; data types of parameters are elementary types whose size matches; minimum, maximum and default are ordered; ParamN and AssemN references resolve; EPATHs decode; assembly members fill their size; keywords are not repeated within a section, and no two ParamN, EnumN, AssemN or ConnectionN keywords name the same number (Param1 and Param01).

#### func (Issue) String

```go
func (i Issue) String() string
```

String returns for example "error: line 4 [Device](#type-device): VendCode missing".
